WF-03 Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0106. Produce the root-cause diagnosis and the EVIDENCE BASE that lets REVIEWER choose between the issue's proposal (a) and (b) -- you are not choosing between them yourself, and you are not implementing anything (WF-03 Step 1 rule 4: diagnosis only, the fix is designed by CODE-DESIGNER).

BACKGROUND: .tool-versions pins elixir 1.18.3-otp-27 / erlang 27.2, but this workstation's PATH toolchain is Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29. main itself therefore fails both halves of `mix letflow.check`: 4 files fail `mix format --check-formatted`, and 14 'a struct for X is expected on struct update' warnings fail `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`. TWO HARD CONSTRAINTS ON HOW YOU WORK:
1. **Do not install anything on this machine.** No winget/choco/scoop, no asdf/mise bootstrap, no downloading-and-running an installer, no `elixir-install` script, no modification of PATH or of anything under Program Files. A system-wide toolchain install is reserved for the human owner of this workstation and is NOT available to this pipeline. If your conclusion is that a host install is the only real fix, that is a legitimate finding -- report it, do not perform it.
2. **Do not fix anything.** No reformatting, no warning fixes, no edits to .tool-versions or mix.exs. The only files you may write are your own two handoff files.

CRITICALLY -- the check ISS-0106 asks for first IS executable here without installing anything, and you are expected to run it: Docker is available on this host (version confirmed above), and docs/anti-patterns.md documents the established Docker recipe for exactly this (throwaway elixir container, repo mounted read-only or read-write, MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 on Git Bash to stop path mangling). Running `mix format --check-formatted` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` inside that image, against this branch's tree, settles empirically whether the four flagged files and the fourteen warnings are artifacts of THIS HOST'S toolchain or genuine defects in the committed code. Mount the repo READ-ONLY, or copy it into the container, so a container-side `mix format` or build cannot write into the working tree; if _build/ or deps/ interfere (they were compiled under OTP 29 and will not load under OTP 27), use a separate build path (MIX_BUILD_PATH or a copied tree) rather than deleting or overwriting the host's _build/deps. Note that .formatter.exs has `import_deps: [:ecto_sql]`, so `mix format` needs the ecto_sql dep present -- deps/ is already vendored in the working tree, and `mix format` reads a dep's .formatter.exs rather than its compiled beams, so a read-only mount should suffice; if it does not, say exactly what failed rather than working around it silently. Tear the container down afterward. Do NOT run `docker compose up` (see docs/anti-patterns.md -- a Postgres container is already running for this checkout and starting another is a documented mistake). No database is needed for either check.

Then answer the questions in the acceptance criteria below. The point of this step is that REVIEWER receives measured facts, not a restatement of ISS-0106's prose.

AC7 -- OPTION SPACE, not a decision: enumerate the resolution options that the measurements above actually support, each with its evidence, its cost, and what it leaves unfixed. result.summary:
HEADLINE, stated first because it overturns the issue's own 'ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, not inferred)' line: ISS-0106 bundles TWO DEFECTS WITH DIFFERENT ROOT CAUSES, and only one of them is toolchain drift.

  * Symptom 1 (4 files fail `mix format --check-formatted`) is NOT toolchain drift. The pinned Elixir 1.18.3/OTP 27 rejects the same four files with byte-identical diffs. These files are unformatted under EVERY formatter version tested. They were made unformatted by three commits that merged to main on 2026-08-20.
  * Symptom 2 (14 struct-update warnings) IS toolchain drift, and cleanly so: 14 warnings under 1.20.3/OTP 29, ZERO warnings under 1.18.3/OTP 27, same tree.

ISS-0106's proposal (a) -- 'install the pinned toolchain and confirm both checks go green with no file changes at all, which would prove the files are correct and only the host was wrong' -- is therefore REFUTED for Symptom 1 and CONFIRMED for Symptom 2. The four files are not correct. Installing the pinned toolchain on this host would leave `mix format --check-formatted` failing on exactly the same four files.

===== AC1 -- REPRODUCE ON THIS HOST =====

Branch feature/WF03-ISS0106-20260821 at d377d41 (this run's own Step 0.5 commit; no source file differs from main).

Toolchain measured, not copied -- `elixir --version`:
  Erlang/OTP 29 [erts-17.0.5] [source] [64-bit] [smp:16:16] [ds:16:16:10] [async-threads:1] [jit:ns]
  Elixir 1.20.3 (compiled with Erlang/OTP 29)
`which elixir mix` -> /c/Program Files/Elixir/bin/elixir, /c/Program Files/Elixir/bin/mix.

`mix format --check-formatted` -> exit 1, '** (Mix) mix format failed due to --check-formatted.' Exactly four files, with these diffs:
  1. lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex -- lines 92 and 98, inside the @moduledoc heredoc. Formatter wants `\"""` where the file has a bare `"""`.
  2. test/letflow/engine/pin_resolver_test.exs -- lines 239 and 322, `lookup = const_lookup(...)` (102 chars) wants wrapping onto a continuation line.
  3. lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex -- line 541, `def merge_effective_pins(a, b, c)` head wants exploding one-arg-per-line.
  4. test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs -- line 516, a 101-char `"entries" => [...]` list wants wrapping.

`mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` -> exit 1, 'Compilation failed due to warnings while using the --warnings-as-errors option'. `grep -c 'is expected on struct update'` = 14. Every warning is that one class; there are no other warnings. Exact sites, extracted from the compiler's own `└─ file:line:col: Module.fun/arity` trailers:
   lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex:843:27      SubProcess.build_completion_multi_from_merge/12
   lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex:563:24   Reconstruction.apply_event/4
   lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:619:25       Transition.dispatch_parallel_gateway/4
   lib/letflow/engine.ex:1785:35                 Engine.dispatch_task_completion_hop_chain/6
   lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex:602:41   Reconstruction.apply_event/4
   lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:691:10       Transition.dispatch_parallel_split/4
   lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex:619:6    Reconstruction.apply_event/4
   lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:779:12       Transition.dispatch_parallel_join/4
   lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex:630:13   Reconstruction.apply_event/4
   lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:845:30       Transition.fire_join/5
   lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex:652:28   Reconstruction.apply_event/4
   lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:876:19       Transition.dispatch_cancel_branch/3
   lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex:820:11   Reconstruction.resolve_pending_events/1
   lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:881:31       Transition.dispatch_cancel_branch/3
By struct: 11 InstanceState, 2 Token, 1 JoinCounter. By file: transition.ex 6, reconstruction.ex 6, sub_process.ex 1, engine.ex 1.

===== AC2 -- REPRODUCE UNDER THE PINNED TOOLCHAIN (the (a) check) =====

NOT BLOCKED. The container ran. `docker pull elixir:1.18.3-otp-27` succeeded (digest sha256:d40cc4144bdb9e2a21afa278d8e036a0b2dcf689cdaaff1e7532bfb568a6e2d5). Container `iss0106-pinned` started with the repo mounted READ-ONLY at /src (`-v //c/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow://src:ro`, MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 per docs/anti-patterns.md), and the tree copied inside the container to /work (mix.exs, mix.lock, .formatter.exs, .tool-versions, lib, test, config, priv, deps -- 24M; _build deliberately NOT copied, so the OTP 29 artefacts could not interfere and the host's own _build was never touched). No `docker compose up` was run and no database was needed.

In-container version, measured: 'Erlang/OTP 27 [erts-15.2.7] ... Elixir 1.18.3 (compiled with Erlang/OTP 27)' / 'Mix 1.18.3 (compiled with Erlang/OTP 27)'. This is the pin exactly.

One real obstacle, reported rather than worked around silently: the first `mix format --check-formatted` in the container failed with 'Mix requires the Hex package manager to fetch dependencies ... ** (Mix) Could not find an SCM for dependency :ecto_sql from Letflow.MixProject'. The vendored deps/ directory was sufficient in content, but Mix refuses to resolve the dependency tree at all with no Hex installed, so `.formatter.exs`'s `import_deps: [:ecto_sql]` could not be honoured. Fixed with `mix local.hex --force` / `mix local.rebar --force` inside the container (a container-local install, not a host install -- and it was torn down with the container). After that the check ran normally.

RESULT 1, FORMAT -- `mix format --check-formatted` under Elixir 1.18.3/OTP 27: **exit 1**. The same four files, in the same order of discovery, with diffs identical character-for-character to the 1.20.3 run: /work/test/letflow/engine/pin_resolver_test.exs (239, 322), /work/test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs (516), /work/lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex (541), /work/lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex (92, 98) -- including the `\"""` heredoc escape that ISS-0106 line 20-22 attributes specifically to 'a formatter behaviour change between Elixir versions'. Elixir 1.18.3's formatter wants that escape too.

RESULT 2, COMPILE -- `mix deps.compile` exit 0, then `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` under Elixir 1.18.3/OTP 27: **exit 0**. `grep -c 'is expected on struct update'` = 0. `grep -n 'warning:'` = no output at all. Output tail: 'Compiling 83 files (.ex) / Generated letflow app'.

EXPLICIT VERDICT ON THE QUESTION ISS-0106 POSES: NO. Both checks do NOT pass with zero file changes under the pinned version. The compile check passes; the format check fails identically. Option (a) as ISS-0106 frames it -- 'confirm both checks go green with no file changes at all, which would prove the files are correct' -- cannot be satisfied, and the reason is that the premise is false: the files are not correct.

===== AC5 (answered here because AC2's result changes what the question is) -- ACTUAL ROOT CAUSES =====

ROOT CAUSE OF SYMPTOM 1 -- three merges landed unformatted code on main on 2026-08-20. Not drift. Established two ways.
(i) Line-level blame, `git log -1 -L <line>,<line>:<file>`, on the exact failing lines:
    lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex:92     -> 91d7e25, 2026-08-20, 'fix(ISS-0080): make VariableMerge's purity self-check measure what it claims, close GH#301'
    lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex:541      -> cb43cc2, 2026-08-20, 'fix(ISS-0078): restore rebind provenance in PinResolver, close GH#299 (#347)'
    test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs:516 -> cb43cc2, same commit
    test/letflow/engine/pin_resolver_test.exs:239 -> a7fa87b, 2026-08-20, 'fix: verify pin_overrides against the injected Lookup instead of trusting them verbatim, close GH#298 (#349)'
(ii) Before/after check per file, using ISS-0008's own `git show <rev>:<path> | mix format --check-formatted -` technique so nothing had to be written to the working tree:
    variable_merge.ex     at 91d7e25^ -> exit 0 | at 91d7e25 -> exit 1
    pin_resolver.ex       at cb43cc2^ -> exit 0 | at cb43cc2 -> exit 1
    pin_rebind_test.exs   at cb43cc2^ -> exit 0 | at cb43cc2 -> exit 1
    pin_resolver_test.exs at a7fa87b^ -> exit 0 | at a7fa87b -> exit 1
Every one of the four was format-clean at its introducing commit's parent and unformatted at that commit. The mechanism is human/agent hand-editing after (or instead of) running `mix format`, merged through a Step Final gate that did not stop it. Note what the content itself says: three of the four failures are ordinary line-length wraps at 101-102 characters, which no formatter version has ever accepted; the fourth is a heredoc escape. This is not a version-sensitive class of diff. The most probable proximate mechanism -- and this is the part that should alarm REVIEWER -- is the exact consequence ISS-0106 line 41-44 predicts in the abstract: 'every agent running a full `mix letflow.check` on this host sees a red gate it did not cause, which invites ... learning to treat a red gate as normal.' Three runs on 2026-08-20 merged past a red format gate. Whether they attributed it to known drift or never ran it is not determinable from the commits alone and is not asserted here.

ROOT CAUSE OF SYMPTOM 2 -- genuine version-specific behaviour. Elixir 1.20's set-theoretic type checker re-infers a private function's parameter types across an unspec'd function boundary and cannot narrow a bare variable to a struct; 1.18.3's checker does not perform this analysis, so the identical source emits nothing. This is exactly the class ISS-0046 (resolved 2026-08-18) fixed for three sites in transition.ex, and ISS-0046 line 44-47 recorded the version attribution as UNCONFIRMED because 'no older Elixir install was reachable to compare.' AC2's container run settles it: CONFIRMED 1.20-only. The 14 current sites are new instances in code that landed after ISS-0046, not a regression of ISS-0046's fix -- its pattern matches are still present in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex (lines 175, 308-309, 329, 343, 391-392, 471, 481-482, 505-506, 538-539, 591).

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT EITHER ONE -- enforcement points inventoried, each measured:
  1. mix.exs line 8: `elixir: "~> 1.18"` (quoted from the file). In Elixir's version syntax a two-component `~> 1.18` means >= 1.18.0 and < 2.0.0 -- it admits 1.19 and 1.20. This host's 1.20.3 satisfies it, so the compile-time backstop never fires. README.md:149-157 (text added by the pin commit 68edfbc) and ISS-0106 lines 36-39 both assert it 'accepts any 1.18.x patch'; that is wrong. `~> 1.18.0` is the form that would restrict to 1.18.x. CATCHES: a host on 1.17 or older. DOES NOT CATCH: this host, or any 1.19/1.20/1.21 host.
  2. .tool-versions (elixir 1.18.3-otp-27 / erlang 27.2, read from the file). Inert unless a version manager reads it. Measured on this host: `which asdf mise rtx` -> all three 'not found' across the full PATH. Also measured: `grep -rn 'tool-versions' lib/ mix.exs test/` finds only prose in two design documents -- no code in this repo reads the file. CATCHES: nothing, on any host without asdf/mise. DOES NOT CATCH: this host at all.
  3. `mix letflow.check`. mix.exs lines 56-60 define it as exactly `["format --check-formatted", "compile --warnings-as-errors", "letflow.check.test"]`. Read lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex in full (120 lines): it shells out to `mix test` and greps for the 'default values for the optional arguments' substring. `grep -rn 'System.version()\|otp_release' lib/ mix.exs config/` returns only two prose lines in lib/letflow/design/decision0005-toolchain-pin-apply.md. NOTHING in the gate inspects the running Elixir or OTP version. CATCHES: the symptoms, loudly. DOES NOT CATCH: the cause -- it reports 'these files are not formatted' with no indication of which toolchain's opinion that is, which is precisely what makes a real defect (Symptom 1) indistinguishable from a version artefact (Symptom 2) at the moment an agent reads it.
  4. CI. `ls -la .github` -> 'No such file or directory'. Confirms 0005's own line 47-49 claim, still true. No enforcement point outside a developer's shell exists.
WHERE IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN CAUGHT, AND WHAT IS ABSENT: Symptom 1 should have been caught at Step Final of runs 91d7e25 / cb43cc2 / a7fa87b, by the format gate that was already there and already correct. What is absent is not a mechanism but a reason to believe the mechanism -- an agent that cannot tell a real format failure from a toolchain artefact has no basis for treating a red format gate as blocking, and a standing background failure trains exactly that. Symptom 2 should have been caught by an enforcement point that does not exist anywhere: nothing in the repo compares the running toolchain to .tool-versions.

===== AC3 -- DIRECTIONALITY =====

SYMPTOM 1: measured, and the answer is that there is NO incompatibility in either direction. Method (working tree never written): copied the tree to scratch/tree (scratch/ is git-ignored, .gitignore:38 '/scratch/'), ran a plain repo-wide `mix format` there under the host's 1.20.3, then `docker cp`'d the four resulting files into the container's /work and re-ran `mix format --check-formatted` under 1.18.3 across the whole /work tree.
  Result: **FORMAT_EXIT=0**. The 1.20.3-formatted output is accepted by 1.18.3's checker.
  Consequence for the decision: reformatting these four files does NOT move breakage onto any other host, because the two formatters agree about this codebase's content. The premise behind AC3's own framing -- that (b) 'merely moves the breakage onto every other host' -- does not hold for the reformat half of (b). The fix is one-way safe and bidirectionally clean.

SYMPTOM 2: measured, and the fix is version-agnostic. Method: applied ISS-0046's own idiom to two of the fourteen sites in the scratch copy -- `defp dispatch_cancel_branch(definition_snapshot, %InstanceState{} = instance_state, branch_id)` and the `%JoinCounter{} = counter ->` clause head in the same function.
  Under 1.20.3 on this host: struct-update warning count went 14 -> 12, and both dispatch_cancel_branch sites disappeared from the site list. The fix works.
  The same patched transition.ex, `docker cp`'d into the container: `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` under 1.18.3/OTP 27 -> **exit 0, zero warnings**; `mix format --check-formatted lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex` under 1.18.3 -> **exit 0**.
  Conclusion: an explicit struct pattern match is ordinary Elixir available in both versions, it is not a 1.20-only construct, and it is format-clean under both. Corroborating evidence from the tree itself: ISS-0046's already-merged version of this same fix is present in transition.ex today and the tree compiles with zero warnings under 1.18.3, so the construct is already proven in-repo under the pin.

===== AC4 -- BLAST RADIUS OF (b) =====

The blast radius is far smaller than ISS-0106 assumes, on both halves.

REFORMAT SET, measured not estimated: `diff -rq` of the whole reformatted scratch tree against the working tree, across lib/, test/, config/, priv/repo/migrations/, and mix.exs, returns exactly FOUR differing files and nothing else:
  lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex
  lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex
  test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs
  test/letflow/engine/pin_resolver_test.exs
ISS-0106 line 57 describes (b) as requiring 'a one-shot repo-wide reformat'. A repo-wide `mix format` under 1.20.3 rewrites four files -- the same four already failing the check. There is no wider reformat hiding behind this. (This also means the reformat is not distinctively part of (b): the same four files need the same four edits under the pinned toolchain, per AC2.)

WARNING SITES: the 14 file:line entries listed under AC1, in four files -- transition.ex (6), reconstruction.ex (6), sub_process.ex (1), engine.ex (1).

CROSS-REFERENCE AGAINST IN-FLIGHT WORK -- `git fetch origin` then `git diff --name-only origin/main...origin/<branch>` for each of the four branches named in this handoff:
  fix/ISS-0096-GH324-pack-resolution-enum: docs/issues/ISS-0096.yaml, lib/letflow/definitions/pack_update_resolution.ex, lib/letflow/design/req041-pack-update-diff-schema.md, priv/repo/migrations/20260817083803_create_pack_update_resolutions.exs, test/letflow/definitions/pack_update_migration_test.exs
  fix/ISS-0099-GH327-handlerkey-verify: docs/issues/ISS-0095.yaml, docs/issues/ISS-0099.yaml, lib/letflow/design/req041-pack-update-diff-schema.md, lib/letflow/design/req057-plugin-interface-registry.md
  fix/ISS-0102-GH330-service-task-method-default: docs/issues/ISS-0102.yaml, lib/letflow/design/service_task.md
  fix/ISS-0103-GH331-service-task-endpoint-optional: docs/issues/ISS-0103.yaml, docs/issues/ISS-0104.yaml, lib/letflow/design/service_task.md
WHICH FILES WOULD CONFLICT: **NONE.** The intersection of {4 reformat files} u {4 warning-site files} with the union of all four branches' changed files is empty. Despite their names, none of these branches touches lib/letflow/engine/ at all -- three of them change only design markdown and issue YAML. ISS-0106 line 48-49's stated reason for deferring ('two of the four files are in areas with recent concurrent work (pin_resolver/pin_rebind)') was true of the 2026-08-20 runs that created the drift, but is not true of the branches in flight now. Caveat, stated as one: this is a measurement of the remote refs as of this run's `git fetch`, and a branch created after it is not covered.

===== AC6 -- HOST INVENTORY (a statement about the PAST, not the present) =====

This section describes what the repo's records show hosts ran ON THE DATES RECORDED. Per docs/anti-patterns.md's 'Treat "unreachable/unavailable in this environment" as expiring' finding, none of it is a claim about what any host runs today. The only present-tense measurement in this whole handoff is this host's own `elixir --version` under AC1.

Two distinct toolchains appear across the corpus, separable by erts build:

===== AC7 -- OPTION SPACE (NOT A DECISION) =====

I am not choosing. The choice amends docs/migration/decisions/0005-pin-formatting-toolchain.md and core-directives.md's Instruction Precedence reserves that for REVIEWER. What the measurements support:

FIRST, A REFRAMING REVIEWER SHOULD APPLY BEFORE READING THE OPTIONS: because Symptom 1 is not version-dependent (AC2) and its fix is bidirectionally clean (AC3), reformatting the four files is NOT a cost of any option. It is required under every option including doing nothing about the pin, and it is required identically whether the repo ends on 1.18.3 or 1.20.3. ISS-0106 accounts for it only under (b); that accounting is wrong and inflates (b) relative to (a).

OPTION (a) -- install and use the pinned 1.18.3/OTP 27 on this host.
  Evidence: AC2 -- under the pin, compile is clean (0 warnings) and format still fails on the same four files with the same diffs.
  What it fixes: Symptom 2 entirely, on this host.
  What it leaves unfixed: Symptom 1 entirely. The four files still need reformatting.
  Cost: a system-wide toolchain install on this workstation. **THIS PIPELINE CANNOT PERFORM IT** -- this handoff forbids installing anything, and my session's own operating rules reserve system-wide install/uninstall for the human owner of the machine. Per the handoff's own instruction ('If your conclusion is that a host install is the only real fix, that is a legitimate finding -- report it, do not perform it'), this is reported as a hard constraint on (a): choosing (a) means asking the workstation owner to install Elixir 1.18.3/OTP 27, and it does not resolve until they do. It also, per AC6, would move this host onto a version no record shows any other host still running.

OPTION (b) -- move the pin forward to 1.20.3/OTP 29.
  Evidence: AC4 -- the reformat is four files, not a repo-wide sweep, and conflicts with zero in-flight branches. AC3 -- the 1.20.3-formatted output is accepted by 1.18.3, so a host still on the pin is not broken by the reformat. AC3 -- the 14-warning fix compiles clean and format-clean under BOTH versions, so it is not a 1.20-only edit either. AC6 -- 1.20.3 is what every host observed since 2026-08-20 actually runs.
  What it fixes: both symptoms, and it needs no software installed anywhere.
  What it leaves unfixed: the enforcement gap. A repo pinned to 1.20.3 with no mechanism that selects or checks 1.20.3 has exactly the enforcement profile that produced ISS-0008, ISS-0068, and this issue. It also amends a signed-off decision record whose sign-off (0005 lines 122-149) reasoned explicitly from 1.18.3 being 'what is live on at least this host today' -- a premise AC6 shows is no longer evidenced.
  Cost: 14 warning-site edits, 4 file reformats, a decision-record amendment, README.md:149-157 and docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md:17 updates, and mix.exs's `elixir:` requirement.

OPTION (c) -- MAKE THE GATE DETECT THE DRIFT (the shape ISS-0106 does not consider). Have `mix letflow.check` compare `System.version()` and `:erlang.system_info(:otp_release)` against .tool-versions and fail fast with an actionable message naming both the expected and the running version.
  Evidence: AC5 point 3 -- measured, nothing in the gate inspects either value; the mechanism does not exist today. AC5's Symptom-1 root cause -- three merges landed unformatted code past a red gate whose redness could not be attributed. This option attacks that directly: it converts an ambiguous red gate into an unambiguous one, so 'the formatter disagrees with these files' and 'you are on the wrong toolchain' stop being the same signal.
  ORTHOGONALITY, stated as the handoff requires: this option makes NEITHER check pass on this host. Run today it would add a THIRD failure (running 1.20.3, pin says 1.18.3) on top of the two existing ones. It is a diagnosis improvement, not a remedy, and it is only coherent once the pin names a version some host actually runs.
  What it leaves unfixed: both symptoms. Strictly complementary to (a) or (b), never a substitute.
  Cost: small -- a few lines in a Mix task plus a .tool-versions parser, and it is the only option that produces a mechanical, exit-code-based enforcement point, which is what core-directives.md's 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures' section says to prefer.

OPTION (d), implied by the AC5 finding and listed because the measurements support it independently of the pin question -- fix Symptom 1 on its own merits (reformat the four files) and correct the mix.exs `~> 1.18` -> `~> 1.18.0` off-by-one-component so the compile-time backstop actually does what README claims. Evidence: AC2 (the files are wrong under every version), AC3 (the reformat is safe in both directions), AC5 point 1 (the operator is wrong). Leaves unfixed: Symptom 2, and note that tightening to `~> 1.18.0` would make THIS host unable to compile the project at all -- which is either the point of a backstop or an unacceptable outcome depending on which of (a)/(b) is chosen, so REVIEWER should treat (d)'s second half as coupled to that choice rather than free-standing.

IS THE CONTAINER A VIABLE ONGOING MECHANISM, OR ONLY A ONE-OFF DIAGNOSTIC? Assessed on the same evidence. As an ongoing way for this host to produce format-clean commits: viable but unnecessary and, on this evidence, pointless -- AC2/AC3 show 1.18.3 and 1.20.3 agree about this codebase's formatting in both directions, so running `mix format` in a container would produce byte-identical output to running it on the host. The container buys nothing for formatting. As an ongoing way to run the COMPILE gate under the pin it is viable and does buy something (it is the only way this host can see a clean `--warnings-as-errors` today without an install), but the friction measured this run is real: `mix local.hex --force` is required inside the container before `.formatter.exs`'s import_deps resolves, a 24M tree copy is needed to keep the working tree read-only, and `mix deps.compile` must run from scratch because host _build artefacts are OTP-29 and unusable. As a one-off diagnostic it was decisive -- it is the only reason this diagnosis could separate the two symptoms at all, and it retroactively settles ISS-0046's UNCONFIRMED version question.

===== AC8 -- SEPARABILITY =====

CONFIRMED, and more strongly than the AC anticipates. The two symptoms are independently resolvable, and in fact are two different defects that share only a failing command.
  * Symptom 2's fix is version-agnostic (AC3, measured both ways: warnings 14->12 under 1.20.3 with the two-site patch; the same patched file compiles with zero warnings and is format-clean under 1.18.3). It can therefore be fixed on its own merits regardless of which way the pin decision goes, and it improves the code under either version -- an explicit struct pattern match is better-typed source, not a version workaround.
  * Symptom 1's fix is ALSO independent, which the AC does not anticipate: since the four files fail under both versions and the reformatted output is accepted by both (AC2, AC3), reformatting them is correct under every option and cannot be invalidated by the pin decision.
  * Consequence for CODE-DESIGNER: the fix design CAN be split, and arguably must be. Symptom 1 (4 files, mechanical, zero design ambiguity, zero conflict with in-flight branches per AC4) and Symptom 2 (14 sites, one established idiom already in-repo from ISS-0046) are both unblocked by the pin decision and can proceed while REVIEWER deliberates. Only the pin/enforcement question -- options (a)/(b)/(c) and (d)'s second half -- actually blocks on REVIEWER, and it is the only part that amends decision record 0005.

===== AC9 -- HYGIENE =====

No software installed on this host. No winget/choco/scoop, no asdf/mise, no PATH or Program Files modification. The only install performed anywhere was `mix local.hex --force` / `mix local.rebar --force` INSIDE the throwaway container, destroyed with it.
Nothing was fixed. No source file, .tool-versions, mix.exs, or .formatter.exs was edited. The two-site struct patch and the repo-wide reformat were both applied only to scratch/tree (git-ignored, .gitignore:38), never to the working tree; the container's mount was READ-ONLY (:ro) and all container-side writes went to its own /work copy. scratch/tree and scratch/host-compile.txt were deleted after use.
TEARDOWN, commands and output: `docker rm -f iss0106-pinned` -> 'iss0106-pinned'. `docker rmi elixir:1.18.3-otp-27` -> 'Untagged: elixir:1.18.3-otp-27 / Deleted: sha256:d40cc4144bdb9e2a21afa278d8e036a0b2dcf689cdaaff1e7532bfb568a6e2d5'. `docker ps -a --filter name=iss0106 --format '{{.Names}}'` -> empty. No `docker compose up` was ever run; no Postgres container was created or touched.
`git status --short` after teardown: ' M handoffs/orchestrator.log', ' M handoffs/registry.json' (both ORCH's pre-existing changes, untouched per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §7), and '?? handoffs/WF03-ISS0106-20260821/step-01-diagnose.json' (this file). No tracked source file modified by me.

issues.description: ISS-0106's stated root cause is wrong for Symptom 1. The four format failures are NOT toolchain drift: Elixir 1.18.3/OTP 27 (the pin) rejects the same four files with byte-identical diffs, including the `\"""` heredoc escape the issue attributes specifically to a 1.18-vs-1.20 formatter change. Proposal (a) as ISS-0106 frames it is refuted -- installing the pinned toolchain would leave the format check failing on exactly the same four files. docs/issues/ISS-0106.yaml lines 30-39 should be superseded (not overwritten -- per docs/anti-patterns.md's 'supersede rather than overwrite' guidance) by whichever run implements the fix.

Three commits merged to main on 2026-08-20 -- 91d7e25 (ISS-0080/GH#301), cb43cc2 (ISS-0078/GH#299, PR#347), a7fa87b (GH#298, PR#349) -- each made a previously format-clean file unformatted, verified per-file by check-formatting the introducing commit and its parent (all four parents exit 0, all four commits exit 1). Three of the four diffs are ordinary 101-102 char line wraps that no formatter version has ever accepted. This is a red format gate being merged past three times in one day, which is the exact consequence ISS-0106 line 41-44 predicts and is a more serious finding than the drift it was filed for. Worth a separate issue and worth REVIEWER asking how those runs' Step Final gates reported.

No enforcement point in this repo compares the running toolchain to .tool-versions. Measured: `mix letflow.check` (mix.exs:56-60) runs format/compile/letflow.check.test and nothing else; lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex (120 lines, read in full) never reads System.version() or :erlang.system_info(:otp_release); no code anywhere reads .tool-versions (`grep -rn 'tool-versions' lib/ mix.exs test/` finds only design-doc prose); asdf/mise/rtx are all absent from PATH on this host; `.github` does not exist. Every mechanism decision 0005 produced is declarative. This is the mechanism-level root cause of the recurrence class and is what AC7 option (c) addresses.

mix.exs:8 is `elixir: "~> 1.18"`, which in Elixir's version syntax means >= 1.18.0 and < 2.0.0 -- it admits 1.19, 1.20 and 1.21. README.md:149-157 (added by pin commit 68edfbc) and ISS-0106 lines 36-39 both state it 'accepts any 1.18.x patch'. The intended form is `~> 1.18.0`. The stated conclusion (the backstop cannot catch formatter drift) is right; the stated mechanism is wrong and understates how weak the backstop is. Note that tightening it would prevent this host from compiling at all, so the correction is coupled to the (a)/(b) choice.

docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md:17 still reads 'Elixir 1.17+ / OTP 26+ (the project was scaffolded on 1.14/OTP 25 via apt...)' -- stale against the pin. Commit 68edfbc updated README.md's Notes section but not this guide, even though 0005's option (b) text names the backend developer guide explicitly as where the convention should be documented. Whichever run implements the fix should update it to whatever the pin ends up being.

ISS-0046's UNCONFIRMED note (lines 44-47, 'Whether this is new in Elixir 1.20 specifically ... is UNCONFIRMED -- this environment only has 1.20.3 available to check against; no older Elixir install was reachable to compare') is now settled by AC2: CONFIRMED 1.20-only. Zero struct-update warnings under 1.18.3/OTP 27 on the identical tree, 14 under 1.20.3/OTP 29. Worth backfilling into ISS-0046 as a resolution addendum so the question is not re-opened by a future run.

ISS-0106 line 48-49 defers the fix partly because 'two of the four files are in areas with recent concurrent work (pin_resolver/pin_rebind)'. Measured against the four in-flight remote branches named in this handoff (`git diff --name-only origin/main...origin/<branch>` for each, after `git fetch`), the intersection with both the 4 reformat files and the 4 warning-site files is EMPTY -- none of those branches touches lib/letflow/engine/ at all. The collision concern was valid for the 2026-08-20 runs but does not apply to the current in-flight set. Stated as of this run's fetch; a branch created later is not covered.
